summary: CRT environment-string table insert (cdecl, args lpString1 = "KEY=VALUE" ANSI string, a2 = forward-to-OS flag). Parses the key at the '=' separator (byte 61) via sub_598569, and either replaces, removes (empty value), or appends the entry in the case-insensitive string table anchored at dword_8D3E90 (grown against bucket end dword_8D3E94 via NullTerminatedIntArrayCopyWithAlloc, rebuilt from the wide-string list dword_8D3E98 via WideCharMultiByteStringConversionWithAllocLoop, or allocated from scratch with MallocWrapperForNhMalloc). Lookup uses CaseInsensitiveStringTableLookup; removal frees the old cell via sub_58AA6F and compacts the array; growth uses sub_58B5D4. When a2 is set, forwards the parsed pair to SetEnvironmentVariableA via a heap copy (Strlen + MallocWrapperForNhMalloc + sub_58FCA0 + NUL split at the '=' position). Returns 0 on success and -1 on parse/allocation failures.

local_names.a2: flag: forward the pair to SetEnvironmentVariableA
local_names.v2: pointer to the '=' character in lpString1
local_names.v3: alias of the '=' pointer used for index arithmetic
local_names.lpMem: table pointer alias for the shrink/grow call
local_names.v10: lookup result; negative values encode the insertion index
local_names.v11: working index / entry count used by grow and compact
local_names.v12: cell cursor used while compacting entries
local_names.v15: heap copy of the key string for the OS forward
local_names.v16: position of the '=' within the heap copy
local_names.v17: old cell value being freed on removal
local_names.v18: preserved '=' position for the key/value split

operations.description: Reject a null lpString1 (-1); locate the first '=' (byte 61) via sub_598569(lpString1, 61); reject with -1 when no '=' is found or when the string starts with '=' (lpString1 == v2).
Record whether the value part is empty (v5 = v3[1] == 0) and preserve the '=' position in v18 for the later key/value split.
When the table pointer dword_8D3E90 has reached the bucket-end pointer dword_8D3E94, grow the null-terminated array via NullTerminatedIntArrayCopyWithAlloc(dword_8D3E90).

If the table is still null: when a2 is set and the wide-string list dword_8D3E98 exists, rebuild the table via WideCharMultiByteStringConversionWithAllocLoop() (a non-zero return fails with -1); otherwise return 0 for an empty value, or allocate fresh 4-byte cells for dword_8D3E90 and, if missing, dword_8D3E98 via MallocWrapperForNhMalloc(4).
Look up the key prefix in the case-insensitive table via CaseInsensitiveStringTableLookup(lpString1, v3 - lpString1), producing the index v10 (v11).

When the key is found (v10 >= 0 and the first table cell is non-null): with a non-empty value replace the cell v9[v10] with lpString1; with an empty value free the old entry v9[v10] via sub_58AA6F and compact the remaining entries left by one cell.
After removal, shrink the table via sub_58B5D4(lpMem, 4 * v11); if the shrink returns null, fall through to the environment-variable forwarding step instead of failing.

Forwarding step (a2 set): measure lpString1 with Strlen, allocate a key copy via MallocWrapperForNhMalloc(v14 + 2), populate it with sub_58FCA0(), NUL-terminate the key at the preserved '=' position, call SetEnvironmentVariableA(v15, value pointer or 0), then free the copy via sub_58AA6F.

For a new key with a non-empty value: derive the insertion index v11 = -v10 when not found, grow via sub_58B5D4(v9, 4 * v11 + 8), store lpString1 at index v11 and a 0 terminator at index v11 + 1, then update dword_8D3E90 to the returned block.
Return -1 on parse and allocation failures and 0 on every success path (including the empty-value no-op).
Called by WideCharMultiByteStringConversionWithAllocLoop (0x00597FAC) when rebuilding the environment table from the wide-string list.
